result.summary: Reviewer verdict FINDINGS at target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930). Scope: result parsing/schema bounds, fallback identity/run IDs, structured JSON handling, stale result rejection. 1 MEDIUM reproduced: Coordinator.complete re-validates the result with resultSchema.parse after merging Git push metadata (+181B) and redaction, so a schema-valid result in the ~61259-61440 byte band is discarded at completion, the run is never stored, the worker ends failed with a misleading 'Worker task timed out', and the non-GitHandoffError path re-pushes every tick (1343 pushBranch calls in 1.6s). 2 LOW: the 60 KiB cap is not present in the JSON Schema shown to the model (bounds advertise ~330KB) and its rejection is reported only as 'Missing or malformed structured result'; an assistant message with both an error and a parseable structured payload completes the run and drops the error (SDK-level reachability, live trigger unverified). Verified sound: stale result.json rejection via run_id, identify() identity overwrite, get_worker_result run_id pass-through, duplicate-completion no-op, untrusted result.git.workspace cannot escape the persistence script. Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json. /workspace/repo unchanged at baseline 5672ead, clean; all probes in /tmp/sfrev.
result.details:
F1 MEDIUM src/coordinator.ts:703,707 (bound src/domain.ts:71-73; retry src/coordinator.ts:510-525): ingest validates the agent payload (safeParse line 589 / fallback parse line 684) but complete() re-parses AFTER merging git branch/commit/base_commit/review_url/persisted/dirty (line 703, measured +181 bytes) and after Redactor.value which can grow a string (+7 bytes for a short-userinfo URL). The 60 KiB refine therefore sees a larger value than the accepted one and throws 'Structured result exceeds 60 KiB; place large reports in artifacts', so store.finish (line 708) and the guest mirror never run. The catch block early-returns only for GitHandoffError (line 518), so fallback()->complete()->pushBranch repeats every tick. Reproduced with local fakes: 61178-byte valid payload with push mode github-app -> state=running and the size error; identical payload with push mode none -> state=completed; 1.6s of ticking -> 1343 pushBranch calls, final state=failed, error='Worker task timed out', store.result()=null, no result.received event. Fix: validate the value that will be stored (validate before line 703, merge git after) or clamp/trim with a warning instead of throwing, and add a post-push attempt latch like the GitHandoffError guard. Why tests miss it: the only size test (tests/core.test.ts:145) rejects a 200657-byte payload, and the fallback/stale tests (tests/lifecycle.test.ts:69-113) use one-line results far below the cap.
F2 LOW src/domain.ts:71 + src/providers/opencode.ts:51 + src/coordinator.ts:597-600: resultSchema.toJSONSchema() emits 1462 bytes with maxLength for every field but no 60 KiB trace (refinements are not JSON-Schema representable), while the advertised bounds sum to ~330KB; an over-cap result fails with the generic 'Missing or malformed structured result' so neither model nor operator learns the cause. Fix: state the cap in bootstrap() and/or add a description, and surface the size issue path in the failure text.
F3 LOW (medium confidence) src/coordinator.ts:589: reply selection prefers a parseable payload over reply.error; SDK declares structured?: unknown independently of error (types.gen.d.ts:243). Reproduced at the coordinator boundary: state=completed, error=null. Whether OpenCode 1.18.31 populates structured on an errored message is unverified (no live server). Fix: prefer the failure path when reply.error is set unless the result came from the current-run file fallback.
Refuted hypotheses: the 65536-byte fallback read cap is not practically reachable (pretty-print inflation only 130-330 bytes at 20-60KB); untrusted result.git.workspace cannot escape src/safety.ts persistence script (probed, no side effect). Not assessed: provider pagination, git-handoff internals, CLI/TUI, HTTP auth, packaging. No credentials in any output.
